author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Houthi rebels in Yemen said they had seized control of Greater and Lesser Hanish, two islands in the southern Red Sea, as fighting in the region widened, The Associated Press reported Monday.

The islands sit near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, a passage connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and an important route for commercial shipping. Control of the territory could give the Houthis a new position near maritime traffic, although the group’s claim was not independently verified in the report.

Saudi-backed forces were trying to retake territory, according to the AP. The report also linked the latest development to a broader escalation in Yemen, where tens of thousands of people have been displaced since fighting intensified this month.

The situation remains fluid, and the reported island seizure could not be confirmed by independent observers. Any change in control or new restrictions near the strait could affect shipping risk assessments and add pressure to an already volatile regional conflict.
dek: Houthi rebels say they seized Greater and Lesser Hanish in the southern Red Sea, a claim that could signal a new front near the Bab el-Mandeb shipping route.
headline: Houthis claim control of two strategic Red Sea islands as Yemen fighting widens
